exposure: Indirect methods for estimating child mortality (model-based Brass methods, empirically based IHME methods, cohort-derived method)
Data classification type (maternal age, time since first birth)
outcome: Performance of indirect methods in estimating child mortality rates
Ability to produce robust past child mortality trends
Ability to produce robust recent estimates
cohort: A simulated population derived from 1950-2010 fertility and mortality rates of the United Nations' World Population Prospects for 82 countries.
finding: The IHME methods, particularly the cohort-derived method, outperform the classical Brass method in producing robust past child mortality trends, with better performance when data are classified by time since first birth.
